newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed seeks longer Russian shares/loans deadline.
newsitem.headline: Lebed seeks longer Russian shares/loans deadline.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed has told President Boris Yeltsin winners of last year's shares-for-loans auctions should not be able to sell their stakes before March 1, Interfax news agency said on Friday.
Under the scheme, through which the state tendered stakes in top companies in exchange for loans to the budget, winners were allowed to sell the stakes from September 1.

Interfax quoted Lebed as saying in his report to Yeltsin that the companies had been sold at prices far below their real value. Sales of stakes of 10-15 percent in these firms by international tenders could bring in tens of trillions of roubles more for the budget, he was quoted as saying.
Interfax said Yeltsin had told Lebed and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin jointly to work on the problem of the shares-for-loans deals and make proposals by October 1.
It said Yeltsin had made the order on August 30.
Privatisation Minister Alfred Kokh, speaking before his appointment, said on September 4 he had no plans to extend the period in which auction winners had to hold the shares.
